reasons: Correctly identifies the real issue: Section 9.4 alone meets the preferred position, but Section 2.1's three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay 'without reduction or termination rights' would negate the 30-day convenience right and refund for the committed volume in a multi-year term — a high-severity deviation under T4C (functionally the walk-away scenario of no effective Customer convenience right).

Redline is valid and effective: it strikes the 'without reduction or termination rights' carve-out and adds a proviso preserving Section 9.4 rights with pro rata reduction of the commitment, resolving the internal conflict without disturbing the compliant Section 9.4 language.

Deterministic check 'Customer convenience termination present' failing is a false negative — the 30-day right lives in untouched p0039; the edit correctly targets only the conflicting commitment clause.

Changed-character ratio of 0.770 is acceptable here: the offending phrase sits at the end of a single short sentence, so removing it and adding the conforming proviso necessarily rewrites much of the clause; the commercial commitment itself is left intact, which is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, correctly cites both sections and the playbook position, uses the required prefix, and matches the concise first-person-plural tone.
